edition: Rahlfs–Hanhart 2006; German Bible Society online running text
authorization: User authorized provisional continuation with Rahlfs–Hanhart; Göttingen not obtained.
scope: Rahlfs–Hanhart 2006 remains the user-authorized provisional base. Focused checks of the publisher’s Greek running text are recorded by chapter. This is an English editorial revision, not a complete critical-text or apparatus verification. Göttingen, full apparatus, independent Greek and human read-aloud reviews remain pending.
historical_records: Existing index and reference records were consulted as historical reference, not proof of fresh complete Greek verification.

chapters.focus: All 21 verses read with focused comparison of pronouns, ambushes, the cross-verse slaughter clause, source images and names, and the final saved-ones declaration
chapters.decision: Modernize ordinary you/your and third-person verbs; render ambushes as plural at 1:7, smooth the emphatic prohibition at 1:13 and explicitly carry the future possess through 1:19. Preserve first-person I heard and third-person He sent, the shift to his dwelling/his heart at 1:3, upward/downward eagle and nest imagery, Idumea/Teman, the 1:9–10 continuation with slaughter and impiety, repeated day phrases and prohibitions, recompense upon the head, wine and descent, possessing former possessors, fire/flame/stubble and bearer of fire, Ephrathah and the accepted 1:21 cadence with saved men ascending from Zion and shall.
chapters.running_text_read: The publisher’s full displayed Greek running text was read through web retrieval after its interactive browser panel failed to display the chapter. Focused comparison covered the recorded features; no printed-apparatus or manuscript collation.
chapters.pending: Review the abrupt second-to-third-person shift at 1:3, conditional and cast-away syntax at 1:5, slaughter-clause attachment, plural peoples/assembly at 1:13, bearer of fire at 1:18, and geographical/deportation relations at 1:19–20. Preserve the passive saved and from Zion at 1:21; do not replace them with saviours ascending onto Zion. Independent Greek, Göttingen/apparatus and human read-aloud reviews remain pending.
